orientation.summary: The Georgia 2015 State Wildlife Action Plan (SWAP) is a comprehensive state-level wildlife conservation strategy prepared by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources Wildlife Resources Division. The document engages with climate change substantively as an 'emerging issue' warranting dedicated sections, a technical team appendix, and integration into species/habitat priorities. It treats climate-driven range shifts as a recognized threat—discussing species moving northward, habitat shifts, sea-level rise impacts on coastal habitats, and the need for connectivity corridors—though it performs mostly qualitative synthesis of external analyses rather than conducting its own quantitative modeling. The plan references vulnerability assessment frameworks (CCVI, AFWA guidance), connectivity modeling outputs (Georgia Greenway Map, Southeast Resilient Landscapes), and climate projections conceptually, but applies none of these to focal species via new quantitative analysis within the document itself.

evidence_index.text: Global Warming/Climate Change Defined as consistent, directed change in climatic conditions at regional scales. Such changes may include increases or decreases in average temperatures, changes in the distribution, frequency, or timing of precipitation, changes in the frequency and intensity of storm events, and changes in sea levels.

evidence_index.text: Climate change is consistent, directed change in climatic conditions at regional scales. Climate change is impacting species and habitats, and these effects are projected to increase substantially over time. These climate-driven changes will profoundly affect our ability to conserve fish and wildlife and their habitats.
